title: deploy: apr binary on Jetson requires GLIBC_2.39
rule: apr binary must run on Jetson (Ubuntu 22.04, aarch64, GLIBC 2.35)

build_environment.features: inference (default minus hf-hub safetensors-compare training visualization zram)
build_environment.command: cargo zigbuild -p apr-cli --release --bin apr --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.35 --no-default-features --features inference

binary.elf_format: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64, dynamically linked

target_environment.headroom: GLIBC 2.35 - 2.29 = 6 minor versions of safety margin

previous_state: apr binary compiled against GLIBC 2.39 (lambda-labs Ubuntu 24.04 default) — failed with 'GLIBC_2.39 not found' on Jetson (GLIBC 2.35 only).
resolution: cargo-zigbuild + zig 0.13.0 + target triple aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.35 produces a binary linked against the older GLIBC ABI. zig acts as the cross-compile sysroot, bundling the older GLIBC stubs. No changes to apr source code needed.
notes: The `.2.35` suffix on the target triple is cargo-zigbuild's syntax for pinning the GLIBC ABI floor.
Used --no-default-features --features inference to avoid feature-gated deps that don't cross-compile (training-gpu, visualization).
trueno-zram-core was excluded — would also exclude it if needed for static-only deployment.
Tested binary is the apr CLI; aprender-serve binary would build the same way.
next_steps: Wire into CI: add `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.35` build job to release workflow
Publish as artifact: attach binary to GitHub release per platform
Document in install path: 'For Jetson / ARM SBCs, download the aarch64-linux-gnu-2.35 release artifact'
